items.title: Google DeepMind melds humans and AI agents to vet Signal's secure messaging techniques
items.summary: Post-quantum handshake and Triple Ratchet get a formal security check
items.raw: Google DeepMind researchers have completed a formal verification of Signal's messaging security, marking what they claim is the first time AI has helped devise a proof that links protocol-level security guarantees to a widely used cryptographic implementation. They did so using AlphaProof Code, a multi-agent framework for formal software specification and verification. AlphaProof Code relies on a human-guided agent that writes a Lean specification, assesses machine code semantics, and crafts an agent-authored proof that the Lean kernel checks against the specification. In this instance, AlphaProof Code verified Signal’s post-quantum PQXDH handshake and Triple Ratchet, thereby validating the design of libsignal's forward secrecy, authentication, post-compromise security, and handshake secrecy. In so doing, the Google/DeepMind team – Swarat Chaudhuri, Andrew Ferraiuolo, Anton Kovsharov, Tej Chajed, Sam Schlesinger, Karn Seth, Jonathan Katz, Charles Sutton, and Pushmeet Kohli – has taken a step toward a challenge the Beneficial AI Foundation issued in April to formally verify the Signal protocol and Signal app with Lean. The AlphaProof Code process involves working with various models to turn Signal's security goals into a human-reviewed mathematical specification. Based on this spec, the researchers assigned Gemini Carbon agents to generate Lean code proving the correctness of the libsignal implementation. After the agents generated 6.5 million lines of Lean code, they undertook an auditing pass and flagged bits that required human review. The result is theoretical in that it assumes perfect cryptography and doesn't guarantee the computational secrecy of bytes. But it's still a meaningful assertion of correctness. "It's a system that is fundamentally built for human AI collaboration," said Swarat Chaudhuri, research scientist at Google DeepMind and a professor at the University of Texas at Austin, in an interview with The Register. Traditionally, said Chaudhuri, you start proving theorems with well-defined problems formulated by a mathematician that get submitted to an AI agent for proof. In this case, the researchers had to figure out what to prove. "In formal methods, we always had this belief that verification is the hard bit," he said. "There's thirty or forty years of work on how to scale up verification. Now we are able to do that. Patrick Steven Yaroch, de 37 anos, desviou o montante de carteiras digitais pertencentes a vítimas de fraudes e hackers investigados pela agência federal. Yaroch atuou no esquadrão de segurança nacional da divisão de Boston do FBI entre 2017 e 2025, e como agente especial supervisor na Divisão de Contrainteligência e Espionagem até meados de 2026. Ele foi preso em 31 de julho, após ter relatado o roubo dos ativos digitais à Divisão de Segurança Nacional (NSD), ao Departamento de Justiça (DOJ) e a funcionários do próprio FBI, em 29 de julho. Os documentos do processo apontam que o homem utilizou o seu acesso privilegiado aos sistemas de gerenciamento para obter senhas de recuperação de algumas carteiras digitais apreendidas. Com essas credenciais, Patrick conseguiu realizar cerca de 100 transferências ilícitas, afetando 35 investigações diferentes. Após drenar esses fundos para as suas próprias carteiras, o ex-agente do FBI tentou lavar o dinheiro convertendo esses ativos originais em outras criptomoedas. Entre novembro de 2025 e janeiro de 2026, Yaroch transferiu dezenas de milhares de dólares para contas bancárias pessoais . items.title: Spyware attacks trend toward hitting just about anyone
items.summary: iVerify’s report Tuesday adds to evidence of spyware’s increasingly indiscriminate targeting.
items.raw: There’s mounting evidence of spyware attacks growing more indiscriminate, leading to more everyday citizens being hit as opposed to traditionally “high-value” targets. The AdFection spyware attacks , which could infect anyone visiting a website that had advertising on it, represented the most recent revelation. And iVerify published a report Tuesday analyzing customer infections and threat notifications from Apple that contributes to the trend. “Conventional guidance on spyware risk focused on people with a public profile, a sensitive job or a role that put them on a government’s radar,” the company said. “Some Apple Threat Notification cases iVerify saw this year don’t fit that pattern.” “In Ottawa, Apple Threat Notifications reached the children of a city bus driver and a stay-at-home mom,” it continued. “In Australia, one went to a limousine driver. None of them had a public profile, a sensitive job or an obvious connection to anyone worth spying on. These cases matter because they show the threat reaching people who had no reason to expect it. For an enterprise, the employees most likely to be hit look much more like the limousine driver than like the CEO.” Part of that is that when spyware attacks are less targeted, they might be more likely to hit those who aren’t as diligently focused on routine cyber hygiene, as opposed to CEOs who are probably regularly upgrading their defenses, iVerify told CyberScoop. Rocky Cole, co-founder of the company, said the change reflects a shift in who’s using spyware. “The vast majority of our detections were mass attacks by criminal groups looking to do purely criminal things,” Cole said. “For the purposes of stealing credentials and selling them on the black market, an executive credential is not necessarily more valuable than a system administrator or even an average employee.” iVerify’s report looked at other trends as well. Among the findings: iVerify didn’t see any devices that were infected by the DarkSword or Coruna iOS exploit kits where users received Apple threat notifications, suggesting that the tech giant might be overly focused on nation-state threats and well-known commercial mercenary spyware like NSO Group’s Pegasus. The rate of spyware infections held relatively steady in 2026, at 1.07 infections per 1,000 iOS consumer scans. “Three in four of this year’s detections were criminal adversaries stealing credentials and cryptocurrency, not state-sponsored actors,” the report said.

items.raw: Google patched nine Chrome flaws, including a V8 vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-125350, that attackers have been actively exploiting in the wild. Google has addressed multiple security vulnerabilities, one of which, tracked as CVE-2026-125350, has been actively exploited in the wild. The vulnerability is a use after free issue that resides in XML and was reported by an anonymous source on November 6, 2026.. “Google is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild.” reads the advisory . A Use-after-free (UAF) is a memory corruption vulnerability that occurs when a program continues to use a piece of memory after it has been released (freed). In simple terms, an application allocates memory to store data, then releases that memory when it is no longer needed. A use-after-free bug occurs when the application later tries to access that same memory location, even though it is no longer valid. Attackers may exploit a use-after-free vulnerability to crash an application and cause a denial-of-service condition, corrupt memory, or, under certain conditions, execute arbitrary code. Depending on the affected component and the nature of the flaw, successful exploitation could also allow attackers to escalate their privileges. The IT giant has not shared further details about how attackers are exploiting the vulnerability or who is behind the attacks. “Access to bug details and links may be kept restricted until a majority of users are updated with a fix. We will also retain restrictions if the bug exists in a third party library that other projects similarly depend on, but haven’t yet fixed.” continues the advisory. CVE-2026-125350 is the eighth exploited Chrome zero-day of 2026. Since the start of the year, Google has addressed the following zero-day flaws exploited in attacks in the wild: February 2026 – CVE-2026-2441 (CVSS score: 8.8) – Use after free in CSS. items.title: Russian Turla group used new toolset to silently pilfer emails from Kazakhstan, Romanian governments
items.summary: Nicknamed “Turla’s Cereal,” the tools target Microsoft Exchange servers and lack many obvious indicators of compromise or malicious telemetry, per a new ESET report.
items.raw: Turla, a notorious cyberespionage group aligned with the Russian government, has been wielding a new, customizable toolset to compromise governments around the world over the past year, including Kazakhstan. The toolset was first discovered in November 2025 by cybersecurity firm ESET, which named it “Turla’s Cereal” as a play on its highly modular, interconnected and “serialized” design. It chains and exploits different legitimate functions across Microsoft Exchange, Windows, and .NET assemblies, which Microsoft has described as “the fundamental units of deployment, version control, reuse, activation scoping, and security permissions for .NET-based applications.” “One of the most interesting aspects of this toolset is what we did not find: external command and control infrastructure,” ESET researcher Matías Porolli wrote in the report , released Tuesday. “Instead — adding insult to injury — the victim’s compromised Exchange server is co-opted to act as the C&C infrastructure.” Illustration of Turla’s Cereal compromise of Microsoft Exchange servers using a modular, stealthy toolset. (Source: ESET) Multiple Western governments and threat intelligence firms have attributed Turla as a part of Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB), which is tasked with gathering intelligence on foreign governments, businesses and organizations. According to MITRE, the group has compromised victims in more than 50 countries, spanning governments, militaries, private-sector companies and research organizations. Porolli said the toolset was found on a compromised Exchange server used by the government of Kazakhstan on Nov. 28, 2025, where it could receive commands, execute in memory, gather intel on the organization and collect certain email messages. Another version found inside a Romanian government agency a month later was configured to target emails sent to or received by the Western powers — the European Union and the North Atlantic Treaty Organization — adversarial with Russia. At the time , Romanian politicians were calling for a NATO mission in the Black Sea to deter what they viewed as Russian aggression. In July, the EU announced sanctions against Russian individuals and organizations, citing a yearslong cyberespionage campaign from Turla and other Russian groups against European nations as well as the targeting of Poland’s energy grid and European businesses by Russia-aligned hacking groups. items.raw: Multiple vulnerabilities have been discovered in SonicWall SonicOS, the most severe of which could allow for Authentication Bypass. SonicOS is the operating system that powers SonicWall firewalls and network security appliances. Successful exploitation of the most severe of these vulnerabilities could allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to perform unauthorized operations, gain elevated privileges, access sensitive information, or impact the integrity of the affected device. An attacker who successfully exploits these vulnerabilities could potentially modify device configurations, access protected resources, bypass security controls, or disrupt normal operations. Organizations with internet-accessible management interfaces may face increased risk from the vulnerabilities affecting the SonicOS management interface.

Os atacantes acederam remotamente aos controladores de refrigeração e alteraram as definições de descongelação para temperaturas elevadas, provocando a perda de alimentos e pelo menos quinze incêndios. O incidente levou as autoridades francesas a ponderar sanções da União Europeia e a protestar formalmente junto do embaixador iraniano.

Para evitar que os alertas se tornem ruído de fundo inútil, é essencial distinguir quais as falhas que afetam diretamente os produtos e sistemas efetivamente utilizados por cada organização.
points: O excesso de alertas de cibersegurança sem contexto pode sobrecarregar utilizadores e empresas.
A existência de uma vulnerabilidade crítica não significa o mesmo nível de risco para todas as organizações.

items.why: Ajuda a otimizar a resposta a incidentes ao focar os recursos em ameaças realmente relevantes para o negócio.

items.title: Claude Code está a expor passwords e chaves secretas no GitHub sem que ninguém repare
items.summary: A ferramenta Claude Code da Anthropic inclui uma funcionalidade que permite aos programadores autorizar comandos de consola sem interrupções constantes. Quando o utilizador escolhe a opção para não voltar a perguntar, a ferramenta regista a instrução aprovada. O problema ocorre quando essa instrução contém credenciais confidenciais, levando à exposição acidental de milhares de dados sensíveis na Internet.
points: O Claude Code permite automatizar a execução de comandos de consola para programadores.
A opção de memorizar instruções regista comandos aprovados sem alertas adicionais.
Credenciais sensíveis incluídas nestes comandos acabam por ser expostas publicamente.
items.why: Demonstra como as ferramentas de produtividade para programadores podem expor inadvertidamente dados confidenciais.
items.todo: Reveja cuidadosamente o histórico de comandos e evite guardar instruções que contenham palavras-passe ou chaves secretas.

items.title: Fireworks AI discloses new breach after cloud provider hack
items.summary: A startup de infraestrutura de inteligência artificial Fireworks sofreu uma violação de segurança depois de atacantes comprometerem um fornecedor de serviços em nuvem terceiro. Através dessa brecha inicial, os intrusos conseguiram aceder às máquinas de desenvolvimento da empresa. O incidente evidencia os riscos associados à cadeia de fornecimento e a fornecedores externos.
points: A Fireworks AI foi alvo de uma nova violação de segurança informática.
Os atacantes comprometeram primeiro um fornecedor de nuvem terceiro.
O acesso permitiu aos intrusos entrarem nas máquinas de desenvolvimento da startup.
items.why: Sublinha a vulnerabilidade das empresas face a falhas de segurança nos seus fornecedores de serviços em nuvem.
items.todo: Audite regularmente a segurança dos fornecedores externos e reforce os controlos de acesso aos ambientes de desenvolvimento.

items.title: What a security leader should tell the CEO about leaked credentials
items.summary: Numa entrevista recente, o diretor executivo da GitGuardian abordou os riscos associados a credenciais vazadas e a responsabilidade pessoal dos líderes de segurança e administrações. O responsável explicou que o medo da culpa muitas vezes esconde erros críticos e detalhou o que deve ser comunicado ao CEO em caso de exposição de chaves. Foram ainda discutidas novas métricas de segurança e o impacto do uso de ferramentas de inteligência artificial.
points: Discussão sobre a responsabilidade pessoal de líderes de segurança perante fugas de credenciais.
O medo de assumir culpas pode esconder erros importantes nas organizações.
Necessidade de adotar novas métricas de segurança para além da contagem de alertas.
items.why: Ajuda os líderes de cibersegurança a comunicarem eficazmente incidentes de credenciais vazadas aos órgãos de gestão.
items.todo: Estabeleça uma cultura de transparência para reportar erros rapidamente e utilize ferramentas de deteção automatizada de segredos.

items.title: France Blames Iran for a Cyberattack That Heated Supermarket Refrigerators
items.summary: O governo francês culpou publicamente o Irão por um ciberataque que provocou o aquecimento de frigoríficos em supermercados do país. Na sequência do incidente, abaixou o embaixador iraniano e anunciou que irá procurar a aplicação de sanções europeias contra os responsáveis. O caso ilustra o impacto de ataques informáticos direcionados a infraestruturas físicas.

O ataque provocou o aumento perigoso da temperatura em frigoríficos comerciais.
O governo francês convocou o embaixador iraniano e pediu sanções europeias.
items.why: Demonstra como os ciberataques estatais podem afetar diretamente infraestruturas do mundo físico e bens essenciais.
items.todo: isole sistemas de refrigeração e controlo industrial da rede pública e reforce a autenticação de acessos.

items.title: Security Flaws Across UK Government Sites Exposed ‘God-Tier’ Information
items.summary: Um investigador de segurança descobriu falhas em códigos de acesso público que colocavam em risco informações privadas em vários departamentos governamentais do Reino Unido. A análise revelou que dados altamente sensíveis estavam vulneráveis devido a desproteções no código disponibilizado. O incidente expôs a fragilidade na gestão de dados por parte de entidades públicas.
points: Investigador descobriu falhas de segurança em códigos de sites governamentais do Reino Unido.
Informação privada e altamente sensível esteve em risco em vários departamentos.
A vulnerabilidade decorria de dados expostos em código publicamente acessível.

items.todo: Faça auditorias regulares aos repositórios de código público para garantir que não contêm dados confidenciais.

items.title: Google Issues Chrome Security Update for Eighth Actively Exploited Zero-Day of 2026
items.summary: A Google lançou atualizações de segurança para corrigir nove vulnerabilidades no navegador Chrome, incluindo uma falha de alta gravidade já explorada ativamente por atacantes. O problema, identificado como CVE-2026-125350, consiste num erro do tipo 'use-after-free' no componente XML. Este tipo de falha ocorre quando um programa tenta aceder a uma zona de memória após esta ter sido libertada.
points: A Google corrigiu nove vulnerabilidades no Chrome, incluindo um zero-day explorado ativamente.
A falha principal (CVE-2026-125350) é um erro de 'use-after-free' no componente XML.
O erro permite explorar falhas de memória através de acessos indevidos.
items.why: Destaca a urgência de atualizar navegadores web para evitar explorações ativas de vulnerabilidades desconhecidas.
items.todo: Atualize imediatamente o navegador Google Chrome para a versão mais recente disponibilizada.

items.title: N-able Takes N-central Cloud Offline After Researcher Discloses 33 Zero-Days with PoC Exploits
items.summary: A empresa N-able retirou temporariamente o seu ambiente em nuvem N-central e apelou aos clientes com servidores locais para os desligarem. A medida preventiva surgiu após a divulgação pública por um investigador de mais de 30 vulnerabilidades coletivamente denominadas Able2Shell. A empresa está a tomar ações urgentes para garantir a segurança dos sistemas afetados.
points: A N-able colocou o N-central Cloud offline de forma preventiva.

A empresa instou os clientes locais a desligarem os servidores até nova ordem.

items.title: CISA Warns of Active Exploitation of OpenSSH, GPUStack, FreeSWITCH, and IBM Flaws
items.summary: A Agência de Cibersegurança e Segurança de Infraestrutura dos EUA (CISA) adicionou quatro novas falhas de segurança ao seu catálogo de vulnerabilidades exploradas ativamente. As falhas afetam o GPUStack, o SignalWire FreeSwitch, o OpenBSD OpenSSH e o IBM Aspera Faspex. Entre as vulnerabilidades inclui-se uma falha de autorização incorreta com pontuação máxima de gravidade.

items.title: Iris Ohyama data breach may expose personal information of 7.7 million people
items.summary: A empresa japonesa Iris Ohyama alertou que uma violação de dados num serviço de nuvem externo poderá ter exposto informações pessoais de 7.7 milhões de clientes da sua subsidiária Iris Plaza. items.title: Polícia Civil de São Paulo sofre suposto ataque cibernético e vazamento de dados
items.raw: Criminosos anunciaram o suposto comprometimento de sistemas internos ligados à Polícia Civil de São Paulo, neste sábado (7). A invasão teria rendido acesso privilegiado máximo aos servidores do Instituto de Identificação Ricardo Gumbleton Daunt (IIRGD) e do “Phoenix”, além do SharePoint utilizado pela instituição. O TecMundo comunicou a SSP sobre o possível ataque; a assessoria afirma que, até o momento, não constatou acesso indevido. “A Polícia Civil iniciou a verificação técnica dos ambientes mencionados na publicação e, até o momento, não constatou acessos indevidos aos bancos de dados. As equipes técnicas seguem monitorando os ambientes e analisando os registros disponíveis. Um inquérito policial foi instaurado para apurar os fatos”, diz a SSP em nota ao TecMundo. Realizado em um fórum ilegal, o anúncio criminoso afirma que cerca de 22 mil credenciais de acesso já teriam sido extraídas dos ambientes afetados – o conjunto completo de informações está à venda por US$ 40 mil, cerca de R$ 220 mil em conversão direta. O Instituto de Identificação Ricardo Gumbleton Daunt (IIRGD), que teve seu sistema supostamente acesso indevidamente, atua na identificação civil e criminal de indivíduos, contando com um acervo de documentos, antecedentes e registros biométricos – em média, realiza cerca de 5 milhões de atendimentos por ano. Já o sistema Phoenix é uma base de identificação de pessoas indiciadas ou procuradas, também armazenando fotografias, impressões digitais, voz e outros dados. Além desses ambientes, os criminosos também alegam ter invadido o SharePoint utilizado pela Polícia Civil, sendo um sistema da Microsoft para compartilhamento interno de arquivos. Suposto mapeamento de endpoints pode ter exposto outras instituições de segurança Segundo os criminosos, autodenominados “bl33dr00t”, a invasão ainda teria possibilitado o mapeamento de “endpoints” para diversos outros órgãos ligados a instituições de segurança pública. Neste contexto, o termo possivelmente se refere a links internos e privados para serviços de acesso restrito, que frequentemente exigem credenciais autorizadas e não são expostos a buscadores comuns – como o Google ou Bing. A lista de instituições que teriam sido afetadas pelo processo de mapeamento de endpoints , segundo os criminosos: Corregedoria Geral da Polícia Civil Departamento de Operações Policiais Estratégicas (DOPE) Divisão de Tecnologia da Informação (DTI), vinculada à DIPOL Departamento de Inteligência da Polícia Civil (DIPOL)

items.title: France blames Iran for supermarket hack meltdowns
items.summary: The 'first cyber offensive campaign carried out purely for the purpose of sabotage on national territory'
items.raw: France has turned up the heat on Iran over destructive cyberattacks targeting refrigeration controllers at more than 700 grocery stores in October, spoiling food and sparking fires. The country vowed to take action using “all available means of response.” The supermarket attacks, which affected Casino, Leclerc, Coopérative U, Metro, Carrefour, and Intermarché groups, started at least 15 fires and caused food losses in the tens of millions of euros, according to a Monday report by France’s Cyber Crisis Coordination Centre (C4). The C4 includes the National Cybersecurity Agency of France, the Directorate General for External Security, the Directorate General for Internal Security, the Directorate General for Armament, and the Cyber Defence Command. “This is an unprecedented campaign in terms of its scale and level of aggressiveness, thus constituting the first cyber offensive campaign carried out purely for the purpose of sabotage on national territory,” France’s Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs said in a statement. All signs point to CyberAv3ngers Both the report and the statement attributed the refrigeration controller hacks to the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ (IRGC) Shahid Kaveh cyber unit. The Shahid Kaveh unit, which French national security officials say is led by Reza Salarvand and Mahdi Lashgarian, is better known by its hacktivist personas, including CyberAv3ngers. This is the same crew suspected of involvement in the July attacks that targeted more than 100 internet-exposed water systems in America. While the US government hasn’t attributed the intrusions to any country or group, private-sector security analysts blamed Iran, and specifically CyberAv3ngers. items.raw: Following recent cyber attacks on French blood banks and European supermarkets, U.S. federal agencies are urging critical infrastructure organizations to immediately secure industrial refrigeration systems against remote tampering and temperature manipulation. Key takeaways Cybercriminals are actively targeting unpatched flaws, misconfigurations, and weak or hard-coded passwords in commercial cold-chain and refrigeration controllers globally. Attackers are gaining remote access to manipulate temperature controls and spoil essential products, such as blood and food. CISA, the FBI, and other U.S. agencies are advising organizations to isolate OT systems, secure or remove remote access, patch critical vulnerabilities, and replace end-of-life devices. Critical infrastructure organizations in the healthcare, chemicals, transportation, and food and agriculture sectors must urgently harden their industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems to protect food, medicines, and other essential products against ongoing cyber attacks. That’s the call from the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and other U.S. government agencies, following a series of alarming breaches against refrigeration systems in French blood banks and European supermarkets . “Every organization that depends on refrigeration and monitoring systems should assume it could be a target,” CISA Acting Executive Assistant Director for Cybersecurity Chris Butera said in a statement. Attackers are remotely targeting electronic-temperature and commercial-refrigeration controllers used in grocery stores and cold storage facilities. They’re looking for unpatched vulnerabilities and other security flaws, such as misconfigurations, according to the agencies. Once attackers gain remote access to these systems, they try to tamper with these machines’ temperature controls to damage their refrigerated products. The temperature changes could also trigger fire hazards. In a joint fact sheet , the agencies recommend organizations immediately take the following steps: Use strong authentication mechanisms and change systems’ default passwords. Keep systems updated and promptly patch critical vulnerabilities. Replace legacy devices that have reached end-of-life status. Identify systems accessible from the internet. items.title: Anthropic lança Claude Mythos 5.2 e Fable 5.2, novas versões de sua IA ‘superpoderosa’
items.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 Mythos 5.2 Anthropic
items.raw: A Anthropic lançou o Claude Mythos 5.2 nesta segunda-feira (9), sua mais nova versão de inteligência artificial de fronteira, apresentada como uma das mais poderosas da empresa. O novo modelo supera o Opus 5.5 em quase todos os testes sintéticos divulgados no anúncio, com resultados superiores em programação, pesquisa, cibersegurança e conhecimentos gerais. Para o público geral, ele chega sob a roupagem do Fable 5.2, com salvaguardas de segurança mais rigorosas. Os testadores dos novos Mythos 5.2 e Fable 5.2 destacam que os modelos conseguem se comunicar de forma mais clara do que as versões anteriores , gerando respostas até 30% mais rapidamente do que as respectivas edições 5.1. Na estreia, os novos modelos também estão disponíveis por um custo menor: US$ 8 (R$ 44,06) por milhão de tokens de entrada e US$ 40 (R$ 220) por milhão de tokens de saída. Além do modo convencional, as novas IAs também estão disponíveis no modo opcional “Fast” , que torna a geração de tokens 2,5 vezes mais rápida, mas pelo dobro do preço original. Por se tratar de modelos de fronteira, o Mythos e o Fable são mais apropriados para projetos elaborados e tarefas que demandam maior capacidade de raciocínio. A Anthropic ressalta que o Claude Opus 5.5 continua sendo a opção mais poderosa para uso cotidiano e orienta a escolha da IA de acordo com a complexidade da tarefa. Em um exemplo de demonstração de capacidade, a Anthropic usou o Fable 5.2 para desenvolver um protótipo de sistema operacional . O modelo coordenou 1.000 agentes menores ao longo de oito dias para escrever, testar e revisar o código. O resultado foi um SO funcional capaz de rodar num notebook, com núcleo e drivers próprios, suporte a gerenciamento de janelas e integração com o próprio Claude. “O Fable 5.2 também pode desempenhar o papel de Consultor, em que modelos como Haiku, Sonnet ou Opus o consultam para ajudar a resolver problemas mais complexos, ou Orquestrador, em que ele delega tarefas mais simples a modelos menores”, descreve a empresa. Nos testes sintéticos apresentados, o Fable 5.2 foi comparado com o Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra e o recente Gemini 4 Carbon . A nova IA da Anthropic supera os demais modelos na maioria dos testes apresentados, mas fica atrás do Opus 5.5 no teste de trabalho de conhecimento (AA-Briefcase v1.1). O Gemini 4 Carbon também sai vitorioso no teste de fluxos de trabalho empresariais (AutomationBench). Mais detalhes sobre a metodologia dos testes estão disponíveis no site da Anthro

items.title: União Europeia processa IBM e outras empresas por falhas em sistema de fronteiras
items.summary: Disputa envolve atrasos no desenvolvimento da plataforma, que coleta dados biométricos de viajantes e busca identificar permanências irregulares no território europeu.
items.raw: A União Europeia (UE) entrou com uma ação judicial contra a IBM , a francesa Atos e o grupo italiano de defesa Leonardo por problemas no desenvolvimento do novo sistema automatizado de controle de fronteiras do bloco. O processo foi iniciado pela agência europeia eu-LISA, responsável pela gestão de grandes sistemas de tecnologia da informação nas áreas de imigração, segurança e justiça. O caso envolve o Sistema Automatizado de Entrada/Saída (EES, na sigla em inglês), plataforma criada para registrar a entrada e a saída de viajantes nas fronteiras europeias. O sistema exige que cidadãos de países de fora da União Europeia digitalizem seus passaportes e forneçam impressões digitais e fotografias durante o controle migratório. Processo envolve atrasos e divergências sobre multas A ferramenta foi implementada a partir de outubro de 2025, em meio à pressão política de países europeus por regras migratórias mais rigorosas. O objetivo é identificar viajantes que permanecem no bloco após o vencimento de seus vistos, reduzir fraudes de identidade e ajudar a combater a imigração ilegal. Em comunicado, um porta-voz da eu-LISA afirmou que o processo trata exclusivamente da fase de desenvolvimento da plataforma e não interfere em seu funcionamento atual. Segundo a agência, o sistema está totalmente operacional em toda a Europa. A instituição também informou que não comentará os detalhes da disputa enquanto o caso estiver em andamento. Segundo o Financial Times, que noticiou a ação inicialmente com base em comunicações internas, o processo ocorreu após o consórcio responsável pelo desenvolvimento perder prazos repetidamente e contestar notificações e multas aplicadas pela agência. Correspondências entre as empresas e a eu-LISA indicam divergências sobre cronogramas e penalidades que remontam a vários anos.

items.title: FORGE Lab uses agentic tools to identify memory safety issues in Rust
items.summary: Microsoft FORGE Lab researchers found memory-safety bugs in Rust's core and std libraries, including cases where safe Rust code can trigger undefined behavior. Using Hyenas, FORGE's frontier research version of codename MDASH, the team investigated three patterns of misplaced trust in unsafe code and what they reveal about Rust's safety guarantees.
items.raw: In this article How we found and validated the bugs Pattern 1: Trusting code not to panic Pattern 2: Trusting user-provided implementations to be correct Pattern 3: Trusting the underlying system Why Rust still matters and advancing vulnerability discovery with AI Rust's high bar is hard to meet but worth keeping Microsoft’s FORGE Lab found several memory safety issues in Rust’s standard library (std and core), including cases where code written entirely in safe Rust can trigger undefined behavior. The research used Hyenas, FORGE’s frontier research version of codename MDASH, an AI-powered vulnerability-scanning system. The findings reveal three recurring patterns of misplaced trust in unsafe code: trusting code not to panic, trusting user-provided implementations to be correct, and trusting the underlying system. Rust’s safety guarantees are precisely what make these findings interesting. Its rich type system and ownership model rule out whole classes of memory-safety issues, but much of the standard library relies on unsafe code underneath its safe APIs. When that code breaks its safety contract, even safe Rust can encounter behavior the language is designed to prevent. Rust’s memory-safety guarantees are increasingly important as the language becomes part of software that billions of people rely on every day. Billions of people are estimated to interact with Rust-based software or operating systems daily, often without knowing it. Microsoft made Rust a Tier-1 internal language alongside C++, C#, and TypeScript, GitHub rewrote the Copilot agent runtime in Rust , and Bun , Android , the Linux kernel , and Cloudflare are moving code to it as well. Much of this software relies on Rust’s foundational libraries, core and std, and the safety guarantees of the APIs they provide. Bugs in those libraries can have consequences well beyond the code where they originate. Unsafe Rust has been a long-running interest for us. Our team includes the people behind Rudra , a static analyzer that looked for memory-safety bugs across the Rust ecosystem in 2021. We also write many of our own tools in Rust, so its safety is more than a research topic for us. This year, we took a closer look at the standard library to see what kinds of mistakes still show up in its unsafe code today. In this post, we share some of the bugs we reported to the Rust issue tracker. We use them to discuss what Rust does and doesn’t guarantee, why writing correct unsafe Rust is so difficult, and why

items.title: Attackers backdoor trusted AWS integrations to steal secrets
items.summary: Wiz researchers uncovered the secret-stealing supply-chain attack
items.raw: Unknown attackers used compromised identity and access management (IAM) credentials associated with Qubole's AWS account to access customer AWS environments, stealing secrets and other sensitive data from S3 buckets. Qubole is a cloud data processing platform that uses cross-account IAM roles to manage compute and access storage in customers' AWS environments without requiring customers to provide long-lived AWS access keys. The supply-chain attack abused this third-party, cross-account trust relationship. Google’s cloud-security shop Wiz declined to tell us how many organizations were affected, but called it a “broad, opportunistic supply chain campaign” that hit “multiple” customer environments. “Because many organizations left trust policies active even after deprecating the platform, the attacker was able to successfully assume integration roles, enumerate cloud resources, harvest secrets, and siphon data,” the researchers told The Register in an emailed response to questions. Neither AWS nor Qubole responded to The Register's inquiries. Wiz, working with Google's Mandiant incident responders after AI data security company Sentra flagged suspicious activity, traced the malicious activity back to October 14, when credentials associated with Qubole's AWS account were used to call the sts:AssumeRole API to obtain temporary credentials for customer-managed integration roles. The calls originated from Qubole AWS account 805246085872, and used IAM user ID AIDA3W7DIFLYOLTK63SFS, Wiz analysts Zack Morrow, Sean Johnstone, and Benjamin Read said in a Monday blog about the supply chain attack. “Across the affected environments, Wiz CIRT has not observed this IAM user in any activity other than that associated with this threat actor,” the trio wrote. This activity continued on October 15, and on October 18, the digital intruders began using a second IAM user from the same account. Once inside customers’ environments, the crooks began probing a ton of AWS services and stealing credentials, keys, and other secrets stored across Lambda, Secrets Manager, and SSM Parameter Store. The miscreants also used TruffleHog to test AWS credentials belonging to victim organizations, discover their Microsoft Entra ID secrets, and request OAuth tokens using Okta client credentials also uncovered while snooping around the AWS environments. items.title: Vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation
items.summary: "*sshole" poses a serious threat to Internet security.
items.raw: Hackers are actively exploiting a recently discovered critical vulnerability that allows them to log in to privileged accounts on many Linux systems, multiple researchers are reporting. The vulnerability, tracked under the name *sshole, arises from the interaction between OpenSSH and a code library known as musl. Linux systems that use both of these packages and meet certain other requirements can be hacked to give unauthenticated access to high-privilege accounts in a matter of seconds. *sshole became publicly known last Thursday and quickly stoked concerns it could lead to widespread compromise of Linux machines. Four days later, the prediction shows signs of becoming real. Attackers conducting "mature intrusions" Security firm Greynoise said Monday that honeypots it maintains in Southeast Asia have come under attack by a group it’s tracking as GT10. The group conducted “mature intrusions" into the systems, which Greynoise uses to detect attempted or successful attacks in real time. Greynoise subsequently gained access to a GT10 server that revealed potential other victims and some of the tools used in the campaign. A backdoor the group is using in the attacks contains Chinese language comments and appears to be generated with the use of AI. Read full article Comments

items.title: France Blames Iran for the Supermarket Fridge Attacks
items.summary: France blames Iran for supermarket fridge attacks. What’s known, what remains unclear, and how to secure exposed controllers. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps was behind the attacks on supermarket fridges in France on 11 and 12 October. He said they hit 700 sites and raised refrigerator temperatures. Some stores threw […]
items.raw: France blames Iran for supermarket fridge attacks. What’s known, what remains unclear, and how to secure exposed controllers. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps was behind the attacks on supermarket fridges in France on 11 and 12 October. He said they hit 700 sites and raised refrigerator temperatures. Some stores threw away their entire stock of perishable food, and fires broke out in several. “France attributes destabilization and sabotage campaigns against French interests to the Islamic Republic of Iran (electronic and cyber center of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of Iran – IRGC-ECC).” reads the announcement published by French cybersecurity agency ANSSI. “Following its investigation, C4 is able to attribute these destructive actions to the Shahid Kaveh cyber-offensive unit, affiliated with the electronic and cyber center of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of Iran (IRGC-ECC): infrastructure characteristics, use of signing tools, relay of the attack by a propaganda organ linked to Shahid Kaveh, traces of the use of Persian in the attack infrastructure.” Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot described the attack as “unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression” and called it the first major cyber sabotage operation on French soil. He promised EU-level sanctions, and France summoned the Iranian ambassador. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the response should be strong, adding that she had only just learned about France’s attribution. “I can confirm that this attack was carried out by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of the Islamic Republic of Iran,” Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said of the cyberattacks on French supermarkets, which occurred on October 11 and 12, and reported Le Monde . “This attack is unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression,” said Barrot. “It marks the first large-scale cyberattack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation’s interests and the security of the French people.” “We will implement sanctions at the European level against all those responsible,” he added. Paris prosecutors opened a judicial investigation into the head of Shahid Kaveh , an offensive cyber unit tied to the Guards’ Electronic and Cyber Center, and his two deputies. items.title: Ajudar a defender contra o envenenamento de memória no Amazon Bedrock AgentCore com validação de escrita em várias camadas
items.summary: A Amazon detalhou como proteger o Amazon Bedrock AgentCore contra o envenenamento de memória, uma forma de injeção indireta de prompts onde atacantes inserem instruções maliciosas na memória de longo prazo de um agente de IA. Para mitigar este risco, a solução propõe combinar controlos nativos já existentes, como políticas IAM, o Cedar e a API ApplyGuardrail, com um novo sinal de desvio semântico baseado em embeddings. Esta abordagem em profundidade ajuda a detetar conteúdos anómalos ou ofuscados sem exigir alterações diretas ao código do agente.

Como: Combinação de controlos AWS IAM, Cedar, Guardrails e validação semântica.
Impacto: Prevenção de comportamentos maliciosos persistentes em agentes de IA.
Quem: Administradores e programadores que utilizam o Amazon Bedrock.

items.why: Protege os agentes de IA contra manipulações persistentes que podem comprometer o seu comportamento futuro.

items.title: Atacantes exploram falha na 'Festa de Escritório' do Claude para executar código malicioso no Linux
items.summary: Investigadores descobriram que atacantes podem tirar partido de uma vulnerabilidade na ferramenta de processamento de documentos do assistente de IA Claude. O vetor de ataque envolve a criação de um ficheiro temporário que o assistente acede e executa automaticamente na máquina do utilizador. Esta falha permite comprometer sistemas operativos Linux através da execução de código não autorizado.
points: O quê: Exploração de falha na ferramenta de documentos do Claude.
Como: Criação de um ficheiro temporário executado pelo assistente de IA.
Impacto: Execução de código malicioso em máquinas com Linux.
Quem: Atacantes que exploram a ferramenta de processamento da Anthropic.
items.title_original: Attackers Crash Claude's 'Office Party' Flaw to Run Malicious Code on Linux
items.why: Mostra como vulnerabilidades em ferramentas de IA assistivas podem ser transformadas em vetores de execução remota de código.
items.todo: Atualize ferramentas de IA e assistentes de desenvolvimento para as versões mais recentes corrigidas.

items.title: Hackers exploram acesso AWS confiável da Qubole para invadir contas de clientes e roubar dados
items.summary: Entre 14 e 26 de outubro, atacantes conseguiram violar contas na AWS pertencentes a vários clientes da plataforma de dados Qubole. O intruso utilizou credenciais de uma conta AWS que a própria Qubole utilizava para interagir com os ambientes dos clientes, embora a forma como obteve esses dados não tenha sido revelada. O ataque resultou no roubo de credenciais armazenadas e de dados confidenciais.
points: O quê: Violação de contas AWS de clientes da Qubole.
Como: Utilização de credenciais de acesso privilegiado da plataforma Qubole.
Impacto: Roubo de dados e segredos armazenados na cloud.
Quem: Atacantes desconhecidos que visaram clientes da Qubole.
items.title_original: Hackers Exploit Qubole's Trusted AWS Access to Breach Customer Accounts and Steal Data
items.why: Ilustra os riscos de segurança associados a acessos de terceiros e cadeias de fornecimento na cloud.
items.todo: Audite regularmente as permissões de acesso atribuídas a fornecedores terceiros e implemente o princípio do privilégio mínimo.

items.title: Empresa russa de cloud Beget reconstrói infraestrutura do zero após ataque com wiper

Os atacantes utilizaram malware do tipo 'data wiper' com o objetivo de apagar dados e paralisar os servidores da organização. A empresa teve de efetuar um restablecimento completo dos seus sistemas.
points: O quê: Ataque com malware destruidor de dados (wiper) a fornecedor de cloud.
Quem: Empresa de alojamento cloud Beget.
Impacto: Destruição total de dados e necessidade de reconstrução da infraestrutura.
Como: Infeção por ransomware/wiper direcionado a servidores.
items.title_original: Russian cloud firm Beget rebuilds from scratch after data wiper attack
items.why: Demonstra a capacidade devastadora de ataques com wipers capazes de destruir infraestruturas cloud inteiras.
items.todo: Mantenha cópias de segurança (backups) imutáveis e isoladas da rede principal para garantir a recuperabilidade.

items.title: Hackers comprometem bee-js da Ethersphere e o Swarm Desktop para distribuir malware rouba-carteiras
items.summary: Atacantes comprometeram os mecanismos de automação de lançamento do projeto Ethersphere para publicar versões maliciosas de duas ferramentas da rede de armazenamento descentralizado Swarm (o bee-js 13.3.0 e o Swarm Desktop 0.56.2). As versões adulteradas executam código para roubar chaves de carteiras de criptomoedas e respetivas passwords guardadas no nó, além de instalarem uma backdoor no sistema.
points: O quê: Distribuição de versões maliciosas de bee-js e Swarm Desktop.
Como: Compromisso da automação de lançamentos do projeto Ethersphere.
Impacto: Roubo de chaves de carteiras digitais e instalação de backdoors.
Quem: Atacantes que visaram utilizadores da rede Swarm.
items.title_original: Hackers Compromise Ethersphere's bee-js and Swarm Desktop to Deliver Wallet-Stealing Malware
items.why: Evidencia o perigo de ataques à cadeia de fornecimento de software e gestão de dependências em projetos descentralizados.
items.todo: Verifique assinaturas e hashes de pacotes de software antes de os instalar ou atualizar em ambientes de produção.

items.title: Investigadores exploram aplicações Android de construtores automóveis para desbloquear carros e buzinar remotamente
items.summary: Investigadores de cibersegurança descobriram falhas em aplicações Android de dois grandes construtores automóveis, permitindo o controlo remoto de veículos na Austrália e nos Estados Unidos. O ataque aproveitou-se de vulnerabilidades na plataforma de identidade ForgeRock, incluindo credenciais de administrador predefinidas ou hardcoded e falhas de travessia de diretórios (path traversal) para contornar defesas WAF. Com estes acessos, conseguiram emitir comandos para abrir portas, acender luzes e acionar buzinas.
points: O quê: Exploração de falhas em apps Android de marcas automóveis.
Quem: Investigadores Shubham Shah e Sam Curry.
Como: Abuso de falhas na plataforma ForgeRock, credenciais por defeito e path traversal.
Impacto: Acesso remoto não autorizado a veículos para executar comandos físicos.
items.title_original: Researchers pwn automakers’ Android apps to remotely unlock cars, honk horns
items.why: Revela graves falhas de autenticação e gestão de APIs em aplicações móveis ligadas a veículos conectados.
items.todo: Elimine credenciais predefinidas ou de testes em ambientes de produção e aplique validação rigorosa de inputs em APIs.

items.title: Claude Code expõe acidentalmente segredos por todo o GitHub
items.summary: Investigadores de segurança da Apiiro descobriram que a ferramenta Claude Code tem estado a divulgar inadvertidamente milhares de segredos confidenciais em repositórios públicos no GitHub. A fuga ocorre devido à forma como o assistente gere os ficheiros de configuração locais, gravando comandos aprovados que contêm dados sensíveis como palavras-passe de bases de dados e tokens de API. Embora estes ficheiros devessem ser ignorados por predefinição, a inclusão de regras parciais tem levado utilizadores a partilhá-los publicamente por lapso.
points: O quê: Fuga massiva de dados sensíveis em repositórios públicos do GitHub.
Quem: Investigadores da Apiiro e utilizadores da ferramenta Claude Code.
Como: Gravação acidental de comandos com credenciais em ficheiros de configuração locais.
Impacto: Exposição pública de palavras-passe, tokens de API e dados de acesso.
items.title_original: Claude Code is accidentally exposing secrets all over GitHub
items.why: Alerta para o risco de ferramentas de automação exporem credenciais sensíveis através de ficheiros de configuração locais.
items.todo: Configure corretamente os ficheiros .gitignore e audite repositórios públicos para garantir que não partilha dados confidenciais.

items.raw: Overview Multiple vulnerabilities in the FrodoBots EarthRover Mini+ firmware (version 6.2.4_6.2.5_0.614.0) may allow remote code execution, unauthorized access to onboard sensors, disclosure of sensitive information, and full compromise of affected devices. Exploitation may enable an attacker to remotely control the rover, access audiovisual streams, or pivot into the user’s network. Description The FrodoBots EarthRover Mini+ is a compact, internet‑connected mobile robot used in educational and consumer environments. The device includes a camera, microphone, motor controllers, and multiple onboard services. Multiple vulnerabilities in the EarthRover Mini+ firmware (version 6.2.4_6.2.5_0.614.0) can allow remote code execution, unauthorized access to onboard sensors, exposure of sensitive data, and complete device compromise. An attacker could potentially take remote control of the rover, access its audio and video streams, or use it to gain a foothold in its network. CVE-2026-121685 : The firmware contains several sets of hard-coded, fleet‑wide credentials, including BasicAuth credentials for an Agora token service, AWS IAM (Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management) access keys, Amazon Web Services Internet of Things Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (AWS IoT MQTT) credentials, and a Slack incoming webhook URL. Agora Token Service is an open source server that generates secure, time‑limited authentication tokens for use with Agora.io’s RTC (Real‑Time Communication) and RTM (Real‑Time Messaging) services. A Slack incoming webhook URL is a unique endpoint that lets external systems send messages into a Slack channel without the need for a full Slack application. These are embedded directly in frodobot.bin and are accessible through static analysis of the publicly downloadable firmware or from any device. Extraction requires no special privileges. CVE-2026-121686 : Unauthenticated remote command execution is allowed via Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT). A firmware method accepts arbitrary shell commands delivered via Amazon Web Services Internet of Things Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (AWS IoT MQTT) messages and executes them as root. Access is gated only by shared Internet of Things (IoT) credentials, with no per‑device authentication, enabling remote code execution (RCE) as root across the fleet. items.raw: For the latest discoveries in cyber research for the week of 9th November, please download our Threat Intelligence Bulletin. TOP ATTACKS AND BREACHES Queens Public Library, a New York City public library system serving approximately 2.3 million residents, was struck by a ransomware attack that encrypted its systems. The incident disrupted public computers, Wi-Fi, checkout equipment, digital media services, and its mobile application, while all 66 branches remained open. Russian web hosting provider Beget sustained a destructive cyberattack on November 1 that wiped data across its cloud infrastructure and disrupted hundreds of websites. The attack affected businesses and public services, with more than 1,000 servers requiring manual inspection before restoration. Some backup data was reportedly destroyed. OPSSHIELD, developer of the Linux security tool cPGuard, disclosed a supply-chain attack after compromised credentials enabled attackers to distribute malicious updates on November 2. Approximately 2,950 customer servers executed the malicious script, which installed a backdoor and collected password hashes, credentials, and sensitive server files. Ukraine’s Air Alert app, an emergency notification service used by millions, was compromised by attackers who distributed false radiation, chemical-threat, and military alerts to Kyiv residents. Developers temporarily suspended notifications. A separate attack affected Russia’s emergency alert application, although both countries reported that their core warning systems remained operational. AI THREATS Check Point Research documented cybercriminals using ARTEX, an AI-powered framework that autonomously discovers and exploits vulnerable systems. Researchers identified 1,608 live, publicly accessible instances. Observed campaigns obtained more than 300 iOS signing certificates and harvested approximately 190,000 gaming credentials, including around 6,000 active accounts. Check Point Research identified Haiou, a jailbreak bundle targeting OpenAI Codex that weakens safeguards and modifies agent instructions to promote an external AI gateway. The package also installs security-related capabilities and appeared on infrastructure associated with cybercrime tools, although researchers did not establish that its developers intended criminal use. items.title: Simplify cross-partition access with AWS IAM outbound identity federation
items.summary: You can now use tokens from AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) outbound federation to assume roles in other Amazon Web Services (AWS) partitions. When your workloads run across AWS partitions such as Commercial, China, GovCloud (US), and European Sovereign Cloud, a workload in one partition might need to access resources or communicate with AWS […]
items.raw: You can now use tokens from AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) outbound federation to assume roles in other Amazon Web Services (AWS) partitions. When your workloads run across AWS partitions such as Commercial, China, GovCloud (US), and European Sovereign Cloud, a workload in one partition might need to access resources or communicate with AWS services in another partition. AWS partitions are hard isolation boundaries with independent instances of AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), so a credential issued in one partition isn’t valid in another. As a result, direct role assumption with sts:AssumeRole doesn’t work across partition boundaries and resource policies can’t reference principals that exist in another partition. AWS IAM outbound identity federation already lets your workloads obtain a short-lived, AWS signed JSON Web Token (JWT) and use it to authenticate to external services. Today, we’re extending it with cross-partition support. Your workloads can now use that same mechanism to federate into another AWS partition. A workload in one partition obtains a short-lived JWT using sts:GetWebIdentityToken and exchanges it for temporary credentials in another partition using sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity with no long-term credentials to store or rotate. This post walks through configuring cross-partition identity federation using Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) data access as an example, but the same steps apply to any cross-partition API call. Important: If your workload requires cross-partition access, consult your compliance team to make sure that your implementation aligns with your regulatory or compliance obligations. A non-exhaustive list of examples are FedRAMP, ITAR, DoD CC SRG, GDPR, and others. Why use IAM outbound identity federation for cross-partition access? IAM outbound identity federation provides several benefits, including: Carry origin identity into authorization decisions – The destination trust policy can condition on the source identity’s context, its AWS account, organization ID ( org_id ), source AWS Region, and principal, so you authorize based on who and where the request originated, not only that a token is valid. Cross-partition audit trail – AWS CloudTrail events in the destination Region include the source principal Amazon Resource Name (ARN), source Region, and a token ID that correlates back to the source Region’s GetWebIdentityToken CloudTrail event. items.title: Microsoft's Azure Linux gets 470-plus security fixes in one almighty patching session
items.summary: A mountain of CVEs, a certificate cleanup, and yet more work for Microsoft's patching teams
items.raw: Microsoft has unleashed a whopper of an update for Azure Linux, packing more than 470 CVE fixes into a single release as the software industry's ever-growing pile of vulnerabilities shows little sign of shrinking. Over the weekend, Microsoft rolled out Azure Linux 3.0.2022 with fixes covering everything from the Linux kernel to open source packages and container software. The changelog runs to hundreds of entries, so anyone planning to read the whole thing might want to put the kettle on. Microsoft's release notes contain more than 470 CVE references, although some vulnerabilities appear multiple times because they affect different packages. So that's not necessarily 470 separate security holes, but it's still an impressive amount of patching for one release. The fixes span OpenSSL, curl, Kubernetes, Docker, QEMU, and a lengthy list of other packages that underpin modern Linux environments. The generic Linux kernel has been updated to version 6.6.161.1. There's also been some housekeeping following the eMudhra certificate incident, tracked as CVE-2026-114406. Microsoft has removed or distrusted root certificates that could validate compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates, while adding checks in Python and Go to reject the affected certificates. It has also preserved SSL.com TLS trust where required, presumably to avoid fixing one certificate headache by creating another. Container infrastructure gets plenty of attention, too, with fixes spanning KubeVirt, containerd, Docker Compose, and other components used to keep cloud workloads running. Several CVEs crop up repeatedly across these packages, helping explain the eye-watering number of entries in the changelog. The release includes less security-focused changes too, including new Dockerfiles, an OpenVMM patch for confidential computing support, fixes for systemd hangs, and adjustments to GRUB Secure Boot metadata. The hefty release comes amid an AI-fueled surge in vulnerability discovery that has left developers struggling to keep up with the resulting patch workload. As The Register reported earlier today, Linux creator Linus Torvalds reckons there may finally be signs that the flood is easing, at least in some corners of the kernel. Torvalds said fixes are now arriving faster than new bug reports in the kernel's eBPF subsystem, although he noted that most other areas haven't reached that point. items.raw: Overview PrestaShop's back-office Performance > Debug mode functionality contains a PHP code injection vulnerability. An authenticated attacker with permission to modify debug-mode configuration can submit crafted cookie configuration values that are written into an executable PHP configuration file. Successful exploitation could allow arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the PHP process. Description PrestaShop is an open-source e-commerce platform for creating and managing online stores. Its back-office Performance configuration includes a Debug mode for developers, which is enabled based on a specified cookie name and value. PrestaShop's debug-mode configuration code inserts the user-controlled values debug_cookie_name and debug_cookie_value into a PHP expression without adequately escaping or sanitizing them for use in PHP source code. The application writes this expression into the PHP define() statement in config/defines.inc.php or config/defines_custom.inc.php . A crafted value can terminate the intended string and introduce attacker-controlled PHP statements. The modified configuration file is loaded during application initialization, causing the injected code to execute on a subsequent request. Exploitation requires an authenticated back-office account with permission to modify debug mode settings and a configuration file writable by the PHP process. Root or operating-system administrator privileges are not required. Cross-site request forgery (CSRF) protection helps prevent unauthorized requests made through another user's session, but does not prevent exploitation by an attacker controlling an account with the required permissions. Injected code executes with the privileges of the PHP process. Affected release versions remain to be confirmed. Impact An authenticated attacker with the required configuration permissions could execute arbitrary PHP code in the security context of the PHP process. This could allow access to application secrets and customer data, modification or deletion of application files and database contents, and disruption of store operations. Operating-system command execution depends on the PHP configuration and available functions. The vulnerability does not independently grant root privileges. Solution PrestaShop version 9.2.1 addresses this vulnerability. Administrators should upgrade affected installations to version 9.2.1 or later. QNAP urges users to update Plex Media Server through the QNAP App Center after reports that threat actors exploited the Plex2Shell vulnerability chain to compromise NAS devices. “QNAP has received reports from some users that Plex Media Server on their NAS appears to have been compromised through these vulnerabilities, and QNAP Technical Support is assisting the affected usersadvisory published by QNAP. ” reads the report published by the vendor. “The QNAP Product Security Incident Response Team (QNAP PSIRT) has confirmed that the vulnerabilities exist only in Plex Media Server; QTS, QuTS hero, and other QNAP operating systems are not themselves affected.” Plex Media Server is designed to make movies, music, and other media available across devices. But when a server is exposed to the internet and runs vulnerable software, it can become an entry point for attackers who have little interest in your film collection. On October 16, 2026, security researcher Zach Main published technical details and proof-of-concept (PoC) code for a vulnerability chain dubbed Plex2Shell. Within a day, researchers had observed attackers using the exploit against an internet-facing honeypot, deploying cryptocurrency-mining malware and proxy software. The incident is a reminder of how quickly a public exploit can be weaponized by threat actors. The chain combines four vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server: CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655, and CVE-2026-96656. Together, they can allow attackers to execute arbitrary code on vulnerable servers without valid credentials, provided the required conditions are met. The code runs with the privileges of the Plex service, giving attackers an opportunity to install additional software and abuse the host. The technical details are available in Main’s original analysis, Plex2Shell . Plex had been notified of the vulnerabilities on July 27 and acknowledged the report on August 4, awarding a bug bounty. The company released fixes in September, before the exploit code became public. The loader does not check the library’s name, executable permissions, digital signature, or symbols. items.title: Who Gives A Crap? Hackers, apparently, after toilet paper maker's customer data exposed
items.summary: UK shoppers caught up in third-party security mess, and nobody knows whether the data was flushed away
items.raw: Toilet paper purveyor Who Gives A Crap has found itself in a bit of a mess after an intruder accessed customer information through a third-party software provider, leaving the company scrambling to clean up a breach affecting shoppers in the UK, US, and Australia. In an email sent to affected customers over the weekend, seen by The Register, the loo roll seller warns that personal information was accessed without authorization after a security incident at an unnamed US-based marketing software provider. The email explains that the intruder gained access to the supplier's systems on October 30. The provider spotted the intrusion the following day and says it secured its systems by November 1, although Who Gives A Crap wasn't told until November 6. It's unclear why the supplier sat on the bad news for another five days before passing it on. The exposed information includes customers' names, email addresses, phone numbers, mailing addresses, and total spending with the company. In other words, someone may now know not only where you live, but just how much of your hard-earned cash you've flushed down the crapper. Payment information, order details, and passwords were not involved, and customers' accounts were not directly accessed. That's something of a relief, although whether the intruder actually made off with the data remains a pressing question. "We don't yet know whether the information was copied or downloaded," the company told customers, adding that it had found no evidence of misuse. In a separate public statement, Who Gives A Crap co-founder and CEO Simon Griffiths confirmed that the incident affected customers across the company's Australian, UK, and US stores. Canadian customers, meanwhile, appear to have escaped this particular toilet emergency, with the supplier reporting that no personal information belonging to shoppers in the country was accessed. Who Gives A Crap says it has since disconnected the provider from its systems, changed access credentials, and begun warning affected customers to watch out for suspicious emails, texts, calls, and other unsolicited communications. "The main concern is scam or phishing messages that use your real details to look convincing," the company warned in its customer email. While Who Gives A Crap has been busy cleaning up, the supplier at the center of this particular stink remains a mystery. items.title: Outlook.com bounces legit emails as Microsoft's authentication crackdown goes sideways
items.summary: Missing DMARC or wobbly SPF means your mail may be treated as suspicious
items.raw: A validation error has stopped Outlook.com from accepting legitimate emails. The problem appears widespread and, according to reports from affected users, can result in non-delivery reports with error codes related to SPF (Sender Policy Framework) validation failures. Other users have reported errors highlighting a lack of DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance) information. The troubles began at the end of last week and appear to be the result of Microsoft tightening the rules (or at least attempting to do so) for accepting emails. The company's consumer email services are affected, and it appears that if a domain doesn't have working SPF or if it has a missing DMARC record, then Outlook.com and its ilk will treat it as suspicious and not accept emails. The rules are designed to deal with spam, bulk senders, and the like. In 2025, Microsoft announced new rules designed to strengthen email authentication for domains sending more than 5,000 emails per day. In addition to DMARC and SPF compliance, DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) was also required. Although this seemed like a good idea to ward off spammers, small senders now appear to be affected. According to complainants in the Outlook forum, a single email with just one line might now be rejected. Furthermore, Microsoft has not issued any advisory to customers explaining how the rules have changed. Although some customers insist their DMARC, SPF, and DKIM settings are compliant, many more have reported that once they set them to Microsoft's preferences, email began flowing once more. SPF must pass for the sending domain (the domain's DNS record should accurately list authorized IP addresses/hosts). DKIM must pass to validate email integrity and authenticity. DMARC must have at least p=none and align with either SPF or DKIM (preferably both). The Register asked the Windows giant for more information, but we have yet to receive a response. To make matters worse, the glitch also appears to be intermittent. A resend attempt might succeed following a rejection. To compound the situation, the rejection error message may also be vague about what caused the bounce in the first place. A moderator in Microsoft's support forum acknowledged the bug and said it was "classified as a service degradation." items.title: 13.3 million people’s medical data exposed; companies pay $300,000
items.summary: The New York AG reached a settlement with Perry Johnson & Associates and four related companies over a 2023 breach.
items.raw: The New York attorney general (AG) has reached a settlement over a medical data breach that affected 13.3 million people after basic security failures. Perry Johnson & Associates (PJ&A) and four related companies have agreed to pay $300,000 and implement extensive security reforms following a breach that exposed personal and medical information belonging to more than 13.3 million people. They face another $9.7 million in penalties if they fail to meet the settlement’s terms. New York AG Letitia James announced the agreement on November 6, alongside the attorneys general of Connecticut, Michigan, and New Jersey. Approximately 4.2 million of the people affected were New York residents. The investigation describes a series of failures: remote access without multifactor authentication , nearly identical passwords circulated by email, sensitive files without file-level encryption, and security software that detected malicious activity but did not alert security staff. The result: the companies only discovered the attack when the attackers contacted them on May 2, 2023, and demanded payment. How many people were affected? The stolen database files contained records associated with more than 13.3 million people, including approximately 4.2 million New Yorkers. Earlier reporting put the number of affected patients at approximately 8.95 million. The settlement documents now give the larger figure of more than 13.3 million. The total could be higher, since the AG found that attackers also accessed files in shared network storage containing personal and health information, but the companies did not review those files to identify additional affected people. The information included: Names, dates of birth, and home addresses. Social Security numbers. Medical record and hospital account numbers. Insurance information. Admission diagnoses and dates of treatment. Clinical information from medical transcriptions, including test results, medications, treatment facilities, and healthcare providers. See if your personal data has been exposed. SCAN NOW Notifications were also slow. PJ&A began contacting clients about the stolen database files in July 2023, and its clients notified affected individuals between October 31, 2023, and February 8, 2024. The New York AG found that the companies violated state requirements to disclose a breach as quickly as possible and without unreasonable delay. items.title: Japanese homeware giant pulls online store after cloud breach puts 7.7M records at risk
items.summary: No reopening date as orders face delays and some customers are told to refuse deliveries to cancel purchases
items.raw: Japanese electronics giant Iris Ohyama has taken down its online store after discovering that attackers may have accessed the personal information of 7.7 million customers, leaving shoppers unable to place orders. The retailer, which sells everything from home appliances and furniture to pet supplies, first disclosed the incident on October 29, a day after discovering a suspicious file on a third-party cloud service used by its Iris Plaza ecommerce operation. Iris Plaza immediately suspended its website and associated systems and began investigating, subsequently confirming unauthorized access. Iris Ohyama has since revealed that the potentially compromised cloud environment contained personal information belonging to approximately 5.8 million registered customers, including former members, and another 1.9 million people who had purchased products without creating an account or participated in promotional campaigns. The potentially exposed information includes names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, gender, and passwords, although the company says the exact information at risk varies between customers. Some of that data, including passwords, was encrypted, but Iris Ohyama hasn't explained what protection was used. It has advised customers who reused their Iris Plaza passwords elsewhere to change them, presumably before someone else gets the opportunity. There is some good news for anyone who has handed over their credit card details, as the retailer says it didn't store payment information in the affected cloud service and that it hasn't been compromised. It remains unclear whether the attackers actually made off with any personal information. In its FAQ, Iris Plaza says it is still investigating the possibility of a data leak and has yet to establish the full extent of the intrusion. Meanwhile, Iris Plaza's website is still down, and the company isn't saying when it'll be back. Orders are also taking longer to ship, while customers trying to cancel a purchase have been told they may have to turn the delivery driver away if their parcel arrives before the cancellation is processed. Fortunately for anyone desperate to buy a new rice cooker, Iris Plaza's stores on Rakuten, Yahoo! Shopping, and auPAY Market are still operating. The company says it has found no evidence that those stores were affected. items.raw: US agencies warn attackers are going after industrial refrigeration controllers. The fixes are basic, and most start with getting them off the internet. CISA, the FBI, HHS, USDA and the Department of Transportation published a joint advisory on attacks against industrial refrigeration controllers and cold chain monitoring systems. The activity is global. Healthcare, chemical, food and transport companies use these systems to watch temperatures, keep logs, run defrost cycles and save energy, including in refrigerated trucks. “The authoring organizations are aware of malicious cyber actors targeting electronic temperature controllers and commercial refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage facilities.” reads the advisory published by CISA. “The actors may exploit vulnerabilities or weaknesses in unpatched or internet-accessible controllers to remotely alter settings and force units into continuous heating and defrost cycles, which can cause widespread inventory loss and equipment hazards.” The targets are electronic temperature controllers and commercial refrigeration controllers used in grocery stores and cold-storage sites. Attackers may exploit flaws in unpatched or internet-accessible controllers to change settings remotely and force units into continuous heating and defrost cycles. In plain terms, someone could cook your freezer from the other side of the world. The agencies identify three ways in: bypassing authentication, injecting arbitrary code, and exploiting weak configurations. Once inside, an attacker can change temperatures, which can shorten equipment life, create a fire hazard and destroy stock. Spoiled products that reach consumers can also create a safety risk. “The actors may exploit vulnerabilities or weaknesses in unpatched or internet-accessible controllers to remotely alter settings and force units into continuous heating and defrost cycles, which can cause widespread inventory loss and equipment hazards.” continues the adviosry. An attacker can also hide the damage. Operators lose sight of current temperatures, and that’s a bad moment to learn a cold room has been warm for hours. CISA’s Chris Butera adds that every organization that depends on these systems should assume it’s a target. items.title: AI doesn’t have to go rogue to break the world
items.summary: AI systems are learning to exploit loopholes in everything from software to tax law. The biggest threat may not be malicious intent, but machines doing exactly what we ask.
items.raw: I want to talk about AI hacking. There are three aspects: people hacking AI systems, people using AI to hack other systems, and AIs hacking systems on their own, not even maliciously. The last two matter more than the first. The third is the weirdest and potentially the most destabilizing. I started writing about this in 2021 and in my 2022 book, A Hacker’s Mind . Back then I said it was mostly still science fiction, but not stupid science fiction. We’re seeing it more and more, especially in the past year. The trends I’m describing don’t require a major breakthrough in AI. They’re starting to happen now, and they’ll happen more often as AIs get better at autonomous problem-solving. And it will involve far more than computer code. AI will hack all sorts of social, economic and political systems. It will find vulnerabilities and exploit them. This is a difference in kind, not just degree. We’re not ready for it, and we need to think about the implications now. This article is adapted from a keynote speech delivered at the DEF CON 34 conference in Las Vegas on August 7, 2026. First, I want to broaden the term “hacking.” The tax code isn’t computer code, but it is code. It’s a series of algorithms with inputs and outputs. It has vulnerabilities, which we call loopholes, and exploits, which we call tax avoidance strategies. Black hat hackers exploit them for profit. We call them accountants and attorneys. What is a hack? One definition: “Something that a system permits, but is unanticipated and unwanted by the designers.” It’s subjective and implies novelty and cleverness. A hack follows the rules of a system but subverts its goals or intent, just as a software hack follows the logic of code while doing something its authors neither anticipated nor wanted. All systems of rules can be hacked, including professional sports, customer reward programs, financial systems and politics. Hacks even work against our cognitive functions. A curved hockey stick is a hack, and we know the name of the man who invented it. Mileage runs were a hack. The filibuster was originally a hack in Roman times. Gerrymandering is a hack. Hedge funds and private equity are full of them. A system is just a set of rules or norms, and the rules aren’t always formal. Even the best-designed rules will be incomplete, inconsistent or ambiguous. As long as people want to subvert a system’s goals, there will be hacks. AIs are becoming hackers.
